frontend_smoke.evidence: In-app Browser offline smoke for the privacy-safe share attribution change. At the default desktop viewport, all 10 free questions were completed with an Earth answer, the preview revealed, and the share card rendered as a 1080x1350 blob with enabled Share image controls and no horizontal overflow. At 390x844, the homepage retained the quiz, hid mobile navigation actions, and had a 390px scroll width with no horizontal overflow. Both loads used script.js?v=20260731-share-attribution-1, kept the production API disabled, and produced no console warnings/errors. The localhost server log contained only local page/assets, including the Earth share template, and no API request. Automated coverage separately verifies that the fixed referral URL contains only utm_source=share_card, utm_medium=referral, utm_campaign=organic_share, and utm_content=result_card and excludes answer, element, email, session, reading, order, and customer identifiers. This digest invalidates the evidence on later frontend changes.

paid_flow_e2e.evidence: Narrow digest waiver for a frontend share-text attribution change that does not alter checkout creation, payment verification, paid-answer submission, webhook handling, queueing, report generation, Resend delivery, or any customer response. The only runtime behavior change is replacing the untagged homepage URL in the existing share text with a fixed privacy-safe referral URL. The native image payload remains files + title + text and still omits a separate url field. Automated coverage verifies the exact four UTM labels and rejects private identifier keys; the complete 37-test Node suite passes. Offline browser QA completed the 10-question Earth preview and generated the 1080x1350 share card with the production API disabled and no console warnings/errors or API requests. No Lemon Squeezy transaction, webhook, report, or email was created; production payment/email E2E remains separately unauthorized, so this waiver is SKIPPED evidence rather than deployment or fulfillment proof. Any later paid-flow digest change invalidates this waiver.
